definitions.open: in the webview: from dispatching a ⌘9 keydown on the document (no OS key event) to the animation frame after the Git log canvas first drew a short hash
definitions.scroll: after every row arrived (row count unchanged for 1 s): fling = top to bottom in 2000 frames, steady = 2 rows per frame for 600 frames; interval = rAF timestamp deltas, share within 16.7 ms judged on fling
definitions.diff: in the webview: from a dblclick on the first log row (the 10,000-changed-line commit) to the frame after the commit tab's diff lines (.pw-diff-line) appeared — includes git.show/git.diff/git.blob and IPC
definitions.branch: from the harness's wall clock just before it runs `git checkout <branch>` in the repository to the webview's wall clock at the frame after the status bar branch name changed
definitions.gutter: in the webview: from dispatching an unsaved one-line edit to perf/typing.rs (5,000 lines, the gutter's HEAD base already loaded) to the frame after a `modified` gutter mark appeared
definitions.typing: 300 one-character inserts at 100 ms intervals (10 chars/s for 30 s) into perf/typing.rs; a 5 ms setTimeout probe runs meanwhile and a block is its callback gap minus 5 ms (WebKit has no Long Tasks API); judged on the longest block; the edits are reverted afterwards (nothing is saved)
definitions.commit_scroll: the harness appends a line to each of the 10,000 files in perf/many; after ⌘0 (webview event) and every row arrived (row count unchanged for 1 s): fling = top to bottom in 1500 frames, steady = 2 rows per frame for 600 frames; share within 16.7 ms judged on fling
definitions.stage: from the harness's wall clock just before it runs `git add <file>` in the repository to the webview's wall clock at the frame after that file's row appeared in the staged group
definitions.memory: phys_footprint of the app instance right after the scenario finished (100k rows loaded, one commit tab and perf/typing.rs open, 10,000 changed files listed); not an idle baseline
definitions.judgement: medians over valid measured runs, except the typing block: it is judged on the largest block of every valid run ("no long task over 50 ms" fails if any run has one); a run whose Git log row count differs from `git rev-list --count --all` fails
definitions.trust: the project is registered untrusted, as if the first-open trust prompt was answered "don't trust" (no prompt is shown): blame uses the native (gix) engine, the git CLI paths of trusted projects are not measured
